_comment: CANVAS.md §4.2 / §5: the canvas dialect the three clients share (markdown.ts parseBlocks(body, {canvas: true}), MessageBodyView.swift, BodyTokenizer.kt), ticking a task line, and keeping the caret when the body is replaced. Block descriptors: heading {level, text}, paragraph {lines}, list {ordered, items}, task {items: [{level, done, text, line}]}, image {alt, attachment_id, line}, hr, codeblock {text}. `text` is what the reader sees of the inline tokens (a link shows its label; emphasis markers are gone). Lines are 0-based.

page_links._comment: M121 (WIKI.md §2.3): links of the canvas dialect (canvases and Docs pages) to a Docs page `[label](page:<uuid>)` and to a file `[label](attachment:<uuid>)` (not an image line). `links`: every link token of the body in order, as {url, label}. With `canvas: false` (a message) they stay text and `links` is empty. The phones join in M122; the desktop reads this section from M121.

containers._comment: M149 (WIKI.md §22.5, §26): callouts, toggles and embedded databases of the canvas dialect (canvases and Docs pages; messages keep them as text). A callout is the lines from `::: callout [icon]` to a line `:::`; a toggle from `::: toggle [title]` to `:::`. Opener: /^:::[ \t]*(callout|toggle)(?:[ \t]+(.*?))?[ \t]*$/ (lower case; the rest of the line, trimmed, is the icon or the title; empty → icon null / title ""). Close: /^:::[ \t]*$/. The close is found by scanning down from the opener counting openers (+1) and closes (-1) and skipping fenced code blocks (a ``` fence that has a closing ``` further down, as everywhere else); an opener without its close is a text line (what follows is read as if it were not there). Inside is read as the top level (lists, quotes, code, tasks, images …); `line` of tasks, images and embeds is the line in the whole body. At most two containers deep (a toggle inside a callout): inside the second one an opener and its close are text lines. A container line ends a paragraph or a list. Embed: a line of its own `![label](page:<uuid>#view=<view id>)` (`#view=…` may be left out: the database's first view; the view id is [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}; the id in lower case). Descriptors as in `blocks`, plus callout {icon, tone, blocks}, toggle {title, blocks}, embed {label, page_id, view_id, line} and quote {}. `tone`: the callout's tint, from `tones` (the icon without U+FE0F looked up; anything else, a custom :name: and no icon are gray).
